transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. I used to love going to dance class, hiking, trying out new recipes... even game night with friends. But now, all of that just feels like a chore. I keep putting those things off, and I don't really know why I don't want to do them anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way about the things you used to enjoy?
It's been a while now. Um, I'd say it started right after a robbery at this festival job I was working. That was about two years and three months ago... so, yeah, it's been going on since then.
Do you still take pleasure in the things you do, even if you don't feel like doing them?

Not really, no. Like I was saying before, they really just feel like chores to me now. Even if I do force myself to go on a hike or show up to game night, I don't get anything out of it. I just barely care about it while I'm doing it, so... no, it doesn't give me that same good feeling it used to.
Do you feel sad or empty most of the time?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty most days. It's more just... that lack of interest I mentioned. I just don't feel much of a drive to do things, but I don't walk around feeling sad all the time.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?
No, not really. My weight has stayed pretty much the same, honestly. I haven't noticed any big drops or gains or anything like that.
Have you noticed any changes in how active or sluggish you feel compared to before you started feeling this way about activities?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I know I'm not doing as much because I just don't have the interest, but... physically, I don't feel sluggish or restless or anything. My actual energy levels are pretty much normal.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about things?
No, I don't. I don't really feel guilty about things, and I wouldn't say I feel worthless, either. That hasn't been an issue for me.
Do you ever think about death or dying?
No, I don't. I haven't had any thoughts about dying or... death, or anything like that. It just hasn't crossed my mind.
Have you noticed any changes in how restless or fidgety you feel compared to before?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I don't really feel restless. I'm not fidgety or pacing around or anything.
Do you feel like you're moving or reacting more slowly than you used to?
No, not really. I think I'm moving at my normal pace. I haven't noticed feeling slowed down or reacting any differently than usual.
Do you feel anxious most of the time?
No, not really. I mean, I guess I get stressed every now and then like anybody else, but... no, I wouldn't say I feel anxious most of the time. It's not a constant thing for me.
Have you ever thought about hurting yourself?
No, never. I haven't ever had any thoughts about hurting myself or anything like that.
Do you think your movements or reactions have changed in any way since you started feeling this lack of interest in activities?
No, I haven't noticed any changes like that. Like I said before, I think I'm moving at my normal pace. It's just the lack of interest in things, but my reactions and all that seem the same.
Do you feel like you're doing more things than usual or trying to do too many things at once?
No, I don't think so. I'm definitely not taking on more than usual. If anything, I'm just kind of getting by day to day. I'm not trying to juggle a bunch of things at once or anything like that.
Do you feel like you're doing things more quickly than usual or rushing through activities?
No, I'm not rushing or doing things faster than normal. Everything just feels pretty much the same as it always has in that regard. I'm just going at my regular speed.
Do you still enjoy spending time with friends and family, or has that become uninteresting to you as well?

No, I still like seeing them. Spending time with my family and friends is still... it's still fine. I haven't lost interest in that. It's mostly just other things I don't feel like doing, but being around the people I care about is still good.
Have you noticed any changes in how quickly or slowly you think, compared to before you started feeling this way?

Well, I have noticed that it's harder to get through things that require focus. Like, when I try to work on catering forms or an application for the Chamber of Commerce, I just end up reading the same line over and over again. And then I get completely stuck on small choices, like what price to put down for something, or even just figuring out which email to answer first. It's like my brain just stalls out.
Do you feel like your thoughts are slower than they used to be?

No, I wouldn't say my thoughts are slower, exactly. It's not like my brain is moving in slow motion or anything. It's just... like I said, it's more about getting stuck or not being able to focus, rather than thinking slowly.
Do you feel like you're doing things more slowly than you used to, even if it's not because your thoughts are slower?

No, I don't think so. Um... physically, I'm moving at the same speed I always have. I'm not walking slower or doing things around the house slower or anything like that. It's really just getting stuck on the mental stuff, like I said.
Do you feel like your body is moving more slowly than normal when you are doing things?
No, not at all. Like I just mentioned, physically I feel like I'm moving at my normal pace. I'm not moving in slow motion or anything.
